easy.def: A line of rings joined together.
examples: The dog is on a chain.
A gold chain.
The bike chain broke.

more.def: A line of metal rings joined together in a row.
examples: The bike chain slipped off.
She wore a gold chain around her neck.
The gate was locked with a chain.

easy.def: A line of things connected.
examples: A chain of stores.
A chain of islands.
A chain of events.

more.def: A group of things that are connected one after another.
examples: A chain of islands lies off the coast.
The food chain starts with plants.
A chain of events led to the surprise.

related.def: To set free from a chain.

easy.def: A seat for one person with a back.
examples: Sit on the chair.
The chair is red.
Pull up a chair.

more.def: A seat for one person, with a back and usually four legs.
examples: She pulled the chair up to the table.
A chair sat by the window.
He fell asleep in the big chair.

easy.def: A person who leads a meeting or a group.
examples: The chairman started the meeting.
The chairman is in charge.
She is the chairman of the club.

more.def: A person who leads a meeting or is in charge of a group.
examples: The chairman called the meeting to order.
She is the chairman of the school club.
The chairman thanked everyone for coming.

easy.def: Something hard to do.
examples: The big puzzle is a challenge.
Tying my shoes was a challenge.
This game is a fun challenge.

more.def: Something difficult that tests your skill or strength.
examples: Climbing the steep hill was a real challenge.
Learning a new language can be a challenge.
The long math problem was a challenge for the whole class.

easy.def: A room.
examples: The king's chamber was big.
The cave had a hidden chamber.
The chamber was dark.

more.def: A room, especially a large or special one, or a closed space.
examples: The king slept in a grand chamber.
The explorers found a hidden chamber in the cave.
A bee's honeycomb has many tiny chambers.

easy.def: A short word for champion.
examples: The champ won the title.
He is the swim champ.
Our team is the champ.

more.def: A short, friendly word for a champion.
examples: The champ held up the trophy.
Our school is the spelling champ.
He is the chess champ at the club.

easy.def: The person or team that wins.
examples: She is the swimming champion.
Our team is the champion.
The champion held up the cup.

more.def: A person or team that has won a contest or a whole season of games.
examples: The champion got a gold medal and a trophy.
Our school is the state champion in spelling.
The chess champion has not lost a game this year.

easy.def: A contest to decide the winner.
examples: We won the championship.
The championship game is tomorrow.
They played in the championship.

more.def: A final contest to find out who is the best team or player.
examples: Our team won the championship this year.
The championship game was tied until the last minute.
She trained hard for the swimming championship.

easy.def: A time when you can do something.
examples: I got a chance to play.
This is your chance.
She wants a chance.

more.def: A time or situation that lets you do something you want.
examples: I got a chance to hold a baby chick at the farm.
This is your chance to ask the scientist a question.
Give the new student a chance to join the game.

easy.def: How likely something is.
examples: There is a chance of rain.
No chance of snow.
He has a good chance.

more.def: How likely it is that something will happen.
examples: There is a chance of thunder this afternoon.
Our team has a good chance of winning the game.
The chance of seeing a whale today is small.

easy.def: To become different, or to make different.
examples: Leaves change color.
I changed my shirt.
The weather changes.

more.def: To become different, or to make something different.
examples: Tadpoles change into frogs as they grow.
She changed her clothes after playing in the mud.
The traffic light changed from red to green.

easy.def: Something that becomes different.
examples: The change was big.
We need a change.
I like this change.

more.def: The act of becoming different, or the result of that.
examples: The change from summer to fall is my favorite time of year.
Moving to a new school was a big change for her.
A change of plans meant we stayed home.

easy.def: Coins that you get back or have in your pocket.
examples: I have change.
She got change back.
He saved his change.

more.def: The coins you get back when you pay with more than the cost, or small coins in general.
examples: The cashier gave me change after I paid with a ten-dollar bill.
I found some change in the couch cushions.
He kept his change in a small jar.

related.def: Able to change, or changing often.

easy.def: A TV or radio station.
examples: Change the channel.
My favorite channel is on.
The channel shows cartoons.

more.def: A station on a TV or radio that shows or plays programs.
examples: Change the channel to the cartoons.
The news channel reported on the storm.
Which channel plays your favorite show?

easy.def: A narrow strip of water.
examples: The ship sailed through the channel.
A channel between the islands.
The channel is deep.

more.def: A narrow body of water that joins two larger bodies of water.
examples: The ship sailed through the narrow channel.
A channel runs between the two islands.
The English Channel separates England from France.

easy.def: A part of a book.
examples: I read a chapter.
The first chapter is short.
This chapter is funny.

more.def: One of the main parts that a book is divided into.
examples: I read two chapters before bed.
The first chapter introduces the main character.
The last chapter of the book was my favorite.

easy.def: A person in a story.
examples: The main character is a dog.
My favorite character is funny.
The characters in the book are kind.

more.def: A person, animal or creature in a story, play or movie.
examples: The main character of the book is a brave girl.
My favorite character in the play is the clown.
The characters in the cartoon are animals.

easy.def: What a person is like inside.
examples: He has a kind character.
Her character is strong.
She showed good character.

more.def: The special qualities that make up how a person thinks and acts.
examples: He showed good character by telling the truth.
Her strong character helped her through hard times.
The character of a person is shown by what they do.

easy.def: To ask someone to pay money.
examples: The shop charges two dollars for juice.
The bus charges a dollar for kids.
They charged us nothing.

more.def: To ask a certain amount of money for something.
examples: The farm charges five dollars to pick a basket of berries.
The museum does not charge children under five.
How much do they charge for a pony ride?

easy.def: To put power into a battery.
examples: I charge my tablet each night.
The toy car needs to be charged.
Mom charged the battery.

more.def: To fill a battery with electricity so it can work.
examples: Plug in the tablet to charge the battery.
The electric car charges overnight in the garage.
My watch charges in about an hour.

easy.def: To run forward fast.
examples: The kids charged out of the door.
The puppy charged across the yard.
He charged down the hill on his sled.

more.def: To rush forward quickly.
examples: The kids charged out the door when the bell rang.
The puppy charged across the yard to greet us.
A rhino can charge at high speed when it is startled.

easy.def: The job of looking after something.
examples: Maya is in charge of the plants.
The teacher is in charge of the class.
Who is in charge here?

more.def: The responsibility for looking after or leading something.
examples: Our coach put Dani in charge of the water bottles.
The captain is in charge of the whole ship.
Who is in charge of the library today?

easy.def: A group that helps people who need help.
examples: The charity gave food.
We gave to charity.
The charity helps animals.

more.def: An organization that helps people or animals in need, often with money or food.
examples: The charity gives food to families in need.
Our class raised money for a charity.
She gave her old coats to charity.

easy.def: A nice quality that makes people like you.
examples: She has a lot of charm.
The little house has charm.
He won us over with his charm.

more.def: A pleasing quality that makes people like you or something.
examples: The old village has a lot of charm.
He won the contest with his friendly charm.
The cottage is full of charm.

easy.def: A small object you wear for good luck.
examples: She wore a charm on her bracelet.
The charm is a tiny heart.
I have a lucky charm.

more.def: A small object that people carry or wear for luck.
examples: She wore a silver charm on her bracelet.
He carried a lucky charm in his pocket.
The charm was shaped like a four-leaf clover.

easy.def: Very nice and pleasing.
examples: The puppy is charming.
We stayed in a charming little house.
She has a charming smile.

more.def: Pleasant and attractive in a way that makes people like it.
examples: The charming village had flowers in every window.
He was a charming host who made every guest feel welcome.
The little cottage looked charming with its blue door.

easy.def: A picture or table that shows facts.
examples: The chart shows the weather.
We made a chart.
The chart has numbers.

more.def: A page of facts shown as a table, graph or picture.
examples: The chart shows how many kids like each fruit.
We made a chart of the weather each day.
The teacher put the chart on the wall.

easy.def: To run after someone to catch them.
examples: The dog chases the ball.
Kids chase each other.
The cat chased the mouse.

more.def: To run after someone or something to try to catch it.
examples: The puppy chased its tail around the yard.
Children chased each other around the playground.
The cat chased a mouse into the barn.

easy.def: Running after something.
examples: The chase was fun.
It was a long chase.
The dog started the chase.

more.def: The act of running after someone or something.
examples: The chase ended when the cat caught the toy mouse.
We played a game of chase.
The chase through the park left us tired.

related.def: A person or animal that chases.

easy.def: To talk in a friendly way.
examples: We chat at lunch.
She chatted with her friend.
The neighbors chatted.

more.def: To talk in an easy, friendly way.
examples: The neighbors chatted over the fence.
We chatted on the bus ride to school.
She chatted with her grandmother on the phone.

easy.def: A friendly talk.
examples: We had a chat.
The chat was short.
I had a nice chat with Grandpa.

more.def: A relaxed, friendly talk.
examples: We had a nice chat over lunch.
She had a quick chat with the teacher after school.
A chat with Grandpa always cheers me up.

easy.def: Not costing much money.
examples: The pencil is cheap.
A cheap toy.
The shirt was cheap.

more.def: Costing little money.
examples: The cheap pencil cost only one coin.
We found a cheap ticket to the zoo.
Apples are cheap this week.

easy.def: To break the rules to win.
examples: Do not cheat at games.
He cheated at cards.
She cheated on the test.

more.def: To break the rules or be dishonest in order to win or get ahead.
examples: It is not fair to cheat on a test.
He cheated at the board game by moving the pieces.
The players agreed not to cheat.

easy.def: A person who breaks the rules to win.
examples: The cheat lost the game.
No one likes a cheat.
He was a cheat in the game.

more.def: Someone who is dishonest in order to win.
examples: Nobody wanted to play with the cheat.
The cheat was caught moving the pieces.
A cheat spoils the game for everyone.

easy.def: To look to see if something is right.
examples: I check my work.
She checked the door.
Check the time.

more.def: To look at something to make sure it is correct, safe, or working.
examples: Please check your answers before you hand in the test.
Dad checked the tires before the long drive.
The nurse checked my ears and my throat.

easy.def: The soft part on the side of your face.
examples: I kissed her cheek.
His cheeks are red.
The baby has round cheeks.

more.def: The soft part of your face below each eye.
examples: Mom kissed me on the cheek.
The cold wind made her cheeks red.
A squirrel stored nuts in its cheeks.

easy.def: To shout to show you are happy.
examples: The crowd cheered.
We cheer for our team.
They cheered loudly.

more.def: To shout loudly to show happiness or to encourage someone.
examples: The crowd cheered when our team scored.
We cheer for the runners.
Everyone cheered for the birthday girl.

easy.def: A shout of joy.
examples: The crowd gave a cheer.
We heard a loud cheer.
A cheer rose up.

more.def: A loud shout of joy or support.
examples: The crowd gave a loud cheer.
A cheer rose when the team came out.
We gave three cheers for the winner.

easy.def: Happy.
examples: She has a cheerful smile.
The room is painted a cheerful yellow.
A cheerful bird sang to us.

more.def: Happy and full of good feelings.
examples: The cheerful bus driver greeted every child by name.
He stayed cheerful even though it rained on his birthday.
The nurse's cheerful voice made the patients feel better.

easy.def: A food made from milk.
examples: I like cheese.
Mice love cheese.
Pizza has cheese.

more.def: A food made from milk that can be soft or hard.
examples: The sandwich had a slice of cheese.
Mice love cheese in cartoons.
Pizza is topped with melted cheese.

easy.def: A person who cooks for a job.
examples: The chef made soup.
The chef wore a tall hat.
The chef cooked our dinner.

more.def: A person whose job is to cook, especially in a restaurant.
examples: The chef made soup for the restaurant.
The chef tasted the sauce.
Our class visited the kitchen to meet the chef.

easy.def: A substance that scientists make or use.
examples: Water is a chemical.
The lab has chemicals.
Do not touch the chemicals.

more.def: Any substance that is made of certain elements and can be used in science, such as salt or soap.
examples: The lab keeps chemicals in labeled bottles.
Salt is a chemical made of two elements.
Chemicals in soap help clean away dirt.

easy.def: A small, round, red fruit.
examples: I eat a cherry.
The cherry is sweet.
Cherries grow on trees.

more.def: A small, round, red fruit with a stone in the middle.
examples: I put a cherry on top of the ice cream.
The cherry tree bloomed in spring.
Birds ate the cherries in the tree.

easy.def: The front of your body between neck and stomach.
examples: My chest hurts.
The heart is in the chest.
He puffed out his chest.

more.def: The upper front part of the body, where the heart and lungs are.
examples: The heart and lungs are inside the chest.
He puffed out his chest with pride.
A bird has red feathers on its chest.

easy.def: A big strong box.
examples: The treasure chest is full.
The pirate chest was locked.
Toys are in the chest.

more.def: A large, strong box with a lid, used for storing things.
examples: The pirate buried a treasure chest.
Blankets are kept in the cedar chest.
The old chest at the foot of the bed holds toys.

easy.def: To crush food with your teeth.
examples: Chew your food.
The dog chews a bone.
She chewed the gum.

more.def: To bite and crush food with your teeth before you swallow.
examples: Chew your food slowly.
The puppy chewed on a bone.
Cows chew grass for hours.

easy.def: A baby chicken.
examples: The chick is yellow.
A chick hatched.
The chick peeps.

more.def: A baby chicken or other young bird.
examples: The chick hatched from its egg this morning.
A fluffy yellow chick followed the hen.
Each chick peeped for food.

easy.def: A farm bird that lays eggs.
examples: The chicken laid an egg.
Chickens eat corn.
A chicken pecked the ground.

more.def: A farm bird that is raised for its eggs and meat.
examples: The chicken pecked at the corn.
Our chickens lay six eggs each morning.
A chicken sat on her nest.

easy.def: Meat from a farm bird.
examples: I ate chicken.
Mom made chicken soup.
We had chicken for dinner.

more.def: The meat of a farm bird that is raised for food.
examples: We had roast chicken for dinner.
Grandma makes chicken soup.
She ate a chicken sandwich.

easy.def: The leader of a group.
examples: The fire chief gave orders.
The chief of the village spoke.
She is chief of the team.

more.def: A person who leads or is in charge of a group.
examples: The fire chief thanked the volunteers.
The chief of police spoke at the meeting.
The village chief welcomed the visitors.

easy.def: Most important.
examples: The chief reason is safety.
Rain is the chief problem.
His chief job is cooking.

more.def: Most important or main.
examples: The chief reason for the trip was to see Grandma.
Corn is the chief crop of the region.
Her chief job is feeding the horses.

easy.def: A young boy or girl.
examples: The child ran to the park.
Each child gets a book.
A child is small and young.

more.def: A young person who is not yet an adult.
examples: Every child in the class got a turn on the swing.
The child found a tiny frog under a rock.
Museums often have special programs for each child.

easy.def: A son or daughter.
examples: Grandma has three children.
Their child is in my class.
She is their only child.

more.def: A person's son or daughter, no matter how old they are.
examples: My grandmother's children are my mom and my two uncles.
Even as an adult, she is still her parents' child.
The bear led her two children across the stream.

easy.def: The time when you are a child.
examples: In my childhood I lived by the sea.
Grandpa told us about his childhood.
She had a happy childhood.

more.def: The time of life when you are a child.
examples: Grandpa told us stories about his childhood.
She spent her childhood on a farm.
In her childhood, she loved to climb trees.

easy.def: A cold feeling.
examples: There is a chill in the air.
I felt a chill.
The chill made me shiver.

more.def: A feeling of being cold, or a cold feeling in the air.
examples: There was a chill in the air that morning.
I felt a chill as I walked outside.
A chill ran down her back at the scary story.

easy.def: To make something cold.
examples: I chill the juice.
Chill the milk.
We chilled the watermelon.

more.def: To make something cool or cold.
examples: We chilled the juice in the fridge.
The cold wind chilled my hands.
Chill the dough for an hour.

easy.def: The part of your face below your mouth.
examples: I rested my chin on my hand.
She has a dimple on her chin.
Milk dripped down his chin.

more.def: The part of the face below the mouth, at the front of the jaw.
examples: He scratched his chin while he thought.
She has a small dimple in her chin.
Cold water dripped from her chin after she drank from the fountain.

easy.def: A thin crisp piece of food.
examples: I eat potato chips.
Chips are crunchy.
He ate a corn chip.

more.def: A thin, crisp slice of food that has been fried or baked.
examples: She ate a bag of potato chips.
Corn chips and salsa made a good snack.
The chips were crunchy and salty.

easy.def: A small broken piece.
examples: There is a chip in the cup.
A chip of wood fell.
A paint chip.

more.def: A small piece that has broken off something.
examples: There is a chip in the edge of the cup.
A chip of paint fell from the wall.
The sculptor swept away the stone chips.

easy.def: To break off a small piece.
examples: Do not chip the plate.
The cup chipped.
The paint chipped.

more.def: To break a small piece off something.
examples: Don't chip the plate when you wash it.
The paint chipped off the old fence.
He chipped his tooth on a hard candy.

easy.def: A sweet brown food.
examples: I love chocolate.
Chocolate is sweet.
The chocolate melted.

more.def: A sweet brown food made from cocoa beans.
examples: I ate a piece of chocolate.
The chocolate melted in the sun.
Chocolate cake was served at the party.

easy.def: Made with the sweet brown food.
examples: Chocolate milk.
Chocolate cake.
A chocolate bar.

more.def: Flavored with or made from cocoa.
examples: We drank chocolate milk.
She baked a chocolate cake.
He ate a chocolate bar.

easy.def: When you pick one thing.
examples: It was a hard choice.
You have a choice of two toys.
Make your choice.

more.def: The act of picking one thing from two or more things.
examples: It was a hard choice between the red and blue shirts.
You have a choice of milk or juice.
Her choice was to take the shorter path.

easy.def: To be unable to breathe because something is in your throat.
examples: I choked on a nut.
He choked on the water.
Chew your food so you do not choke.

more.def: To have trouble breathing because something is blocking your throat.
examples: He choked on a piece of bread.
Chew slowly so you do not choke.
The smoke made her cough and choke.

easy.def: To pick one thing.
examples: Choose a book.
I chose the red one.
She chooses a flavor.

more.def: To pick the one you want from two or more.
examples: You may choose a snack from the basket.
She chose the blue bike.
Choose a partner for the game.

easy.def: To cut something into pieces.
examples: Dad will chop the onions.
We chop wood.
She chopped the carrots.

more.def: To cut something into pieces with a quick, hard stroke.
examples: Mom chopped the onions for the soup.
He chopped wood for the campfire.
The chef chopped the herbs into tiny bits.

easy.def: A helicopter.
examples: The chopper flew overhead.
We saw a chopper land.
The chopper carried the doctor.

more.def: A word that people sometimes use for a helicopter.
examples: The chopper flew over the field.
We watched a news chopper circle above the city.
The chopper landed on the roof.

easy.def: A holiday on December 25 when many people give gifts.
examples: We decorate a tree at Christmas.
Christmas is in winter.
I sang songs at Christmas.

more.def: A holiday on December 25 that Christians celebrate for the birth of Jesus, when many families also give gifts.
examples: Our family bakes cookies and gives gifts at Christmas.
Lights and wreaths decorate the town before Christmas.
We sang carols at the school concert near Christmas.

easy.def: To throw something without much care.
examples: I chucked the ball.
He chucked the paper away.
She chucked a pebble.

more.def: To throw something in a quick, casual way.
examples: He chucked the ball over the fence.
Chuck the old papers in the bin.
She chucked her backpack on the couch.

easy.def: To laugh quietly.
examples: I chuckle at the joke.
Grandpa chuckled.
She chuckled to herself.

more.def: To laugh softly to yourself.
examples: Grandpa chuckled at the funny story.
She chuckled quietly while she read.
I could hear my dad chuckle at the cartoon.

easy.def: A building where Christians pray.
examples: We go to church on Sunday.
The church has a bell.
The church is old.

more.def: A building where Christians gather to pray and worship.
examples: The church bell rings on Sunday.
We went to a wedding at the church.
A tall steeple rises above the church.
